classes.name: Quantity_Color
classes.summary:
This class allows the definition of an RGB color as triplet of 3 normalized floating point values (red, green, blue).
Although {@link Quantity_Color | `Quantity_Color`} can be technically used for pass-through storage of RGB triplet in any color space, other OCCT interfaces taking/returning {@link Quantity_Color | `Quantity_Color`} would expect them in linear space. Therefore, take a look into methods converting to and from non-linear sRGB color space, if needed; for instance, application usually providing color picking within 0..255 range in sRGB color space.

instanceMethods.name: Name
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the name of the nearest color from the `Quantity_NameOfColor` enumeration.

instanceMethods.name: SetValues
instanceMethods.comment: Updates the color from specified named color.

instanceMethods.name: SetValues
instanceMethods.signature: (theC1: number, theC2: number, theC3: number, theType: Quantity_TypeOfColor): void
instanceMethods.comment: Updates a color according to the mode specified by theType. Throws exception if values are out of range.

instanceMethods.name: Rgb
instanceMethods.comment: Return the color as vector of 3 float elements.

instanceMethods.name: Red
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the Red component (quantity of red) of the color within range [0.0; 1.0].

instanceMethods.name: Green
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the Green component (quantity of green) of the color within range [0.0; 1.0].

instanceMethods.name: Blue
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the Blue component (quantity of blue) of the color within range [0.0; 1.0].

instanceMethods.name: Hue
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the Hue component (hue angle) of the color in degrees within range [0.0; 360.0], 0.0 being Red. -1.0 is a special value reserved for grayscale color (S should be 0.0).

instanceMethods.name: Light
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the Light component (value of the lightness) of the color within range [0.0; 1.0].

instanceMethods.name: ChangeIntensity
instanceMethods.comment: Increases or decreases the intensity (variation of the lightness). The delta is a percentage. Any value greater than zero will increase the intensity. The variation is expressed as a percentage of the current value.

instanceMethods.name: Saturation
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the Saturation component (value of the saturation) of the color within range [0.0; 1.0].

instanceMethods.name: ChangeContrast
instanceMethods.comment: Increases or decreases the contrast (variation of the saturation). The delta is a percentage. Any value greater than zero will increase the contrast. The variation is expressed as a percentage of the current value.

instanceMethods.name: IsDifferent
instanceMethods.comment: Returns TRUE if the distance between two colors is greater than `Epsilon()`.

instanceMethods.name: IsEqual
instanceMethods.comment: Returns TRUE if the distance between two colors is no greater than `Epsilon()`.

instanceMethods.name: Distance
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the distance between two colors. It's a value between 0 and the square root of 3 (the black/white distance).

instanceMethods.name: SquareDistance
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the square of distance between two colors.

instanceMethods.name: Delta
instanceMethods.signature: (theColor: Quantity_Color, DC: number, DI: number): { DC: number; DI: number }
instanceMethods.comment:
Returns the percentage change of contrast and intensity between this and another color. <DC> and <DI> are percentages, either positive or negative. The calculation is with respect to this color. If <DC> is positive then <me> is more contrasty. If <DI> is positive then <me> is more intense.
@returns A result object with fields:
- `DC`: updated value from the call.
- `DI`: updated value from the call.

instanceMethods.name: DeltaE2000
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the value of the perceptual difference between this color and `theOther`, computed using the CIEDE2000 formula. The difference is in range [0, 100.], with 1 approximately corresponding to the minimal perceivable difference (usually difference 5 or greater is needed for the difference to be recognizable in practice).
